title: Rev. Harold L. Webb & Rev. Thomas Miller v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Judicial complaint by Rev. Harold L. Webb and Rev. Thomas Miller against Pacific Presbytery regarding its August 4, 1975 meeting conducted without the constitutionally required quorum of three teaching and three ruling elders. The Committee on Judicial Business determined the actions were irregular but recommended dismissal after Pacific Presbytery met in duly constituted session on September 10, 1975, with proper quorum and ratified all actions from the August 4 meeting.

title: Session of Eastland Presbyterian Church, Memphis, Tennessee v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found invalid; McKeown was not employed in ministerial capacity
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Judicial Commission found the complaint of Eastland Presbyterian Church against Covenant Presbytery invalid because the presbytery employed Mr. Tim McKeown in a summer worker capacity, not as a minister. The decision clarifies that employment in a non-ministerial capacity does not violate church constitution, even if ministerial employment would have.

title: Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Case returned to lower court with instructions for new hearing; inadequate record
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Session of Trinity Presbyterian Church, Slidell, Louisiana complained that Grace Presbytery violated proper procedure when it delayed the ordination of Adrian Pater, a licentiate who had been examined and sustained for ordination as an evangelist. The Judicial Commission found that inadequate minutes were presented and returned the matter to Grace Presbytery for a new hearing, while recommending that the General Assembly affirm that the BCO does not envision ordination expressly to pastoral services in churches of other denominations.

title: Rev. Paul L. Karlberg and Ruling Elder James G. Luce v. Central Georgia Presbytery

title: Teaching Elders Byron Snapp and James M. Hope v. Calvary Presbytery
disposition_detail: Error sustained; ordination matter remanded to Calvary Presbytery for correction
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.

title: Teaching Elder Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension
disposition_detail: sustained in part (Count 2 sustained; Count 1 split 10-5; remanded to Presbytery for correction and re-examination)
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Carl W. Bogue et al. complained against the Presbytery of the Ascension's sustaining of ordination trials for Mr. Sam Serio and approval of his call to a campus ministry. The Commission remanded the matter for re-examination of Serio and securing a proper call.

title: Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Standing Judicial Commission addressed three issues regarding actions of Covenant Presbytery involving TE Daniel R. Morse and Grace Presbyterian Church. The Commission ruled that teaching elders Morse and Crenshaw, having renounced communion with the PCA by joining the Reformed Episcopal Church, should be removed from presbytery rolls under BCO 38-3. The Commission found no provision requiring churches to notify presbytery before withdrawing from the PCA. Finally, the Commission determined that receiving and recording a protest is an administrative act, not a judicial decision, and that complaints regarding such actions are barred by BCO 45-5.

title: Hopper v. James River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Robert D. Hopper, pastor of Grace Covenant Church in Williamsburg, Virginia, challenged James River Presbytery's April 1991 action forbidding him from preaching and teaching views affirming that the extraordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit (including prophecy and tongues) may be present in the church in the present age. The Standing Judicial Commission denied the complaint, holding that presbytery has constitutional authority under BCO 13-9 and 34-5 to restrict teaching and preaching when it determines such views may be harmful to the spiritual welfare of the churches under its care, and that such restriction does not violate liberty of conscience absent a determination that the forbidden teaching is heretical.

title: Western Carolina v. Tennessee Valley
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Western Carolina Presbytery and two other presbyteries requested the General Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over a teaching elder regarding allegations that women preachers filled the pulpit at Cedar Springs Presbyterian Church. The Standing Judicial Commission dismissed the matter as not properly before the General Assembly, ruling that the conduct of worship services is under the jurisdiction of the Session, not subject to process against a minister under BCO 34-1, and that Tennessee Valley Presbytery did act on the allegations.

title: Tan v. South Texas Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.

title: Fitzsimmons v. Evangel
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.

Fitzsimmons of the time and place of the hearing on his appeal and in failing to adjudicate the appeal once it was found to be in order. The case was remanded to Evangel Presbytery for proper rehearing and adjudication in accordance with BCO 42-8.

title: Rountree v. Covenant
disposition_detail: Appeal denied; divestiture without censure sustained
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Covenant Presbytery properly divested Teaching Elder Lawrence Rountree without censure after he remained on presbytery rolls for over seven years without a valid call to ministry, residing outside presbytery bounds, with no prospects for ministry. The Standing Judicial Commission sustained presbytery's divestiture action as constitutional and appropriate.

title: Shive v. Central Carolina
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained in part; remanded on censure issue only
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC reversed the session's imposition of excommunication on Dr. Robert Shive for inappropriate conduct while counseling female patients, remanding instead for indefinite suspension from the Sacraments, finding insufficient evidence of contumacy or impenitence to justify the highest censure.

title: Adams v. Northeast Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: TE Philip J. Adams complained about a Northeast Presbytery judicial matter while a related appeal was pending and sought a retrial of charges on which the accused had been acquitted. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order under BCO 43-1 and because the requested relief was unavailable. A separate opinion concurred in the result but dissented from part of the reasoning and urged clarification of appellate review after an acquittal.

title: Staley v. North Texas
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint filed by Thomas Clark Staley against North Texas Presbytery to be out of order on the grounds that Mr. Staley had no standing as he was not a member of a PCA church. The decision turned on the jurisdictional requirement that only PCA church members may bring complaints before the Standing Judicial Commission.

disposition_detail: Presbytery action and subsequent commission acts annulled for unauthorized replacement of the Session

The SJC sustained the complaint, held that the presbytery lacked authority to take that action under the BCO and Preliminary Principle Six, and annulled the commission's subsequent acts.

The case was therefore remanded to Presbytery for a new trial in compliance with BCO 32.

standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Larry Ball complained that Westminster Presbytery erred in approving a plan to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC affirmed that a presbytery has the constitutional right to withdraw from the PCA as part of historic American grass-roots Presbyterianism, subject to proper procedures. The court held that the relationship between General Assembly and presbytery mirrors that between presbytery and local church, protecting each level's distinct identity and civil operations.

title: W.W. Marshall Jr. v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery

The word 'taken' refers to any appeal whether past, current, or pending, and ECP's action rescinding its prior judgment was therefore improper.

summary: Complaint by TEs Hutchinson and Bulkeley against Western Carolina Presbytery's Inman Commission opinion regarding views of RE Payne expressed in a November 26, 2007 e-mail. The SJC found that Presbytery did not err because it would be inappropriate for the SJC to render judgment on the Biblical character of a man's views expressed in an e-mail without a more complete statement of those views and proper due process.

title: Morton H. Smith v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Answered by reference to the SJC decision in Case 2008-15
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.

title: Morton Smith v. Western Carolina
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Complaint of TE Morton H. Smith vs. Western Carolina Presbytery. The SJC sustained Smith's complaint in part, finding that Presbytery erred procedurally by immediately adopting a judgment against RE Payne's views without process. The SJC annulled the declaration made by Presbytery regarding RE Payne's views and remanded the case for proper adjudication.

title: Leissing v. Western Carolina
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: RE Henry Leissing complained that Presbytery erred when it voted on November 7, 2008 to reverse the Sealy Commission's October 23 decision and dissolve the calls of REs Linton and Pellom. The SJC sustained the complaint by reference to its decision in Case 2008-15, Issue 5, holding that Presbytery erred in appointing the Sealy Commission in the first place since the underlying August 7 congregational meeting was illegitimate.

title: Payne v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specifications not sustained; BCO 31-2 investigation and no-strong-presumption finding affirmed
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: TE Martin Payne and related complainants challenged Western Carolina Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations concerning TE Craig Bulkeley and its conclusion that no strong presumption of guilt existed. The SJC denied the specifications, holding that BCO 31-2 gives the investigating court great discretion over procedure and timing and that the record did not show clear error; related complainants lacked standing.

title: Bordwine v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; presbytery's declaration reversed and matter remanded for counsel or BCO 31-2 action
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE James Bordwine and others challenged Pacific Northwest Presbytery's handling of study reports on TE Peter Leithart's Federal Vision-related teachings and its refusal to declare those views either orthodox or out of accord with the Standards without judicial process. The SJC sustained the complaint, held that presbytery erred in declaring the views not out of accord, and remanded for pastoral counsel or BCO 31-2 action; concurring and dissenting opinions were recorded.

title: Urish v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Rocky Mountain Presbytery sustained a candidate's ordination exam who held the view that women could teach (but not preach or exercise authority) in church ministries under the authority of the church session. TE James Urish complained that Presbytery erred in sustaining the candidate's exam. The SJC affirmed Presbytery's decision, finding no clear error, as neither the Westminster Standards nor the BCO explicitly address this specific application of 1 Timothy 2:12.

title: Linton v. Western Carolina Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: The Standing Judicial Commission affirmed that Presbytery of Western Carolina did not err in conducting its BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley or in finding no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC found no constitutional error in Presbytery's procedures and gave great deference to the lower court's discretionary judgment, noting that BCO 31-2 does not mandate specific procedures for investigations. The SJC also held that complainants Kirk Lyons and Robert Woodward lacked standing to bring complaints under BCO 43-1 and 11-4.

title: Lyons v. Western Carolina Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Kirk Lyons and others complained that Western Carolina Presbytery erred when it did not find a strong presumption of guilt against TE Craig Bulkeley in a 31-2 investigation, and violated due process by failing to interview the accusing parties. The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint in part, finding that the Presbytery had denied the complainants due process by not allowing them to present evidence before finding no strong presumption of guilt.

title: Woodward v. Western Carolina Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Robert Woodward, along with James Linton and Kirk Lyons, filed complaints against Western Carolina Presbytery alleging it erred when it did not find a strong presumption of guilt against TE Craig Bulkeley and when it failed to properly investigate grievances due to procedural failures and alleged denial of due process to the accusers. The cases were combined with Case 2009-5 (TE Martin Payne complaint) due to similar circumstances.

title: Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Southwest Florida Presbytery denied Paul Armes's complaint on the grounds that his excommunication removed his standing; the SJC unanimously remanded the case to the Presbytery after the Presbytery conceded error, holding that even an excommunicated person retains standing to complain against the censure itself.

standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.

standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.

title: Robinson v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
disposition_detail: Judicially out of order; no merits opinion located
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC catalog records Robinson v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery as judicially out of order, without a merits opinion. The local corpus contains no fuller decision text.

title: Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaints of TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery (cases 2007-09 and 2007-10). KEP erred when it empowered the Pulpit Commission to act on behalf of the church session without proper consent, and erred when it filed a civil action against TE Lee to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The decision affirms the non-hierarchical, voluntary nature of the PCA and its limited jurisdiction in civil matters.

title: McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery
disposition_detail: Administratively out of order; no merits opinion located
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.

title: Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Southwest Florida Presbytery denied Armes's second complaint as a mere restatement of Case 2009-12; the SJC sustained the complaint and remanded, finding the second complaint involved distinct post-censure acts (the trespass notice) that could not be dismissed as identical in substance. A dissenting opinion argued Armes, as an excommunicated person, lacked standing to bring any complaint beyond the limited access afforded under BCO 38-1.

title: McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: McNeil complained that Chesapeake Presbytery erred in denying his complaint against the Session's refusal to receive his charges against his wife after the Session had already censured him for abusive behavior; the SJC denied the complaint, applying a standard of great deference to the lower court and finding no clear procedural error.

title: Koerkenmeier v. Illiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Illiana Presbytery appointed a Commission with broad powers to 'deal with matters' at Center Grove Presbyterian Church; the SJC found this was constitutional error because the language exceeded proper oversight bounds, but declared the error harmless since the Commission acted only as an investigating committee and the Session itself endorsed the Commission's findings.

title: Phelps v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Complainant alleged that Pacific Presbytery erred in not opposing the ordination of Lee Irons as a Ruling Elder at New Life Burbank, given that Pacific Presbytery had previously denied Irons's application as a Teaching Elder candidate; the SJC denied the complaint, holding that each court retains discretion to evaluate candidates for ordination within its jurisdiction and that Presbytery's denial for Teaching Elder did not preclude a Session's ordination of the same man as Ruling Elder.

title: Brown v. Northern California Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

title: Cutler v. Platte Valley
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Complaint of Dale Cutler against Platte Valley Presbytery. The case was found to be administratively out of order and not proceeded with on the merits.

title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.

title: Sartorious et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: The SJC denied a complaint that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in finding no strong presumption of guilt in TE Joshua Moon after an investigation into allegations that his theological views on Federal Vision topics were heterodox, holding that deference to the presbytery was required absent clear error in the record. The case generated a concurring opinion offering procedural guidance on BCO 31-2 investigations versus BCO 32-2 charges, and a dissenting opinion by RE Haigler arguing the record showed unambiguous heterodoxy warranting a finding of strong presumption of guilt.

title: Carpenter v. Siouxlands
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC found that Presbytery of Siouxlands erred in denying a complaint that sought the appointment of a committee to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation into whether TE Greg Lawrence held or taught views associated with Federal Vision theology contrary to the PCA's doctrinal standards. The Court directed that the presbytery conduct the required investigation and established that credible reports affecting Christian character warrant investigation regardless of the evidentiary standards required for conviction.

title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Mr. Sherfey's complaint against James River Presbytery was ruled judicially out of order with defects that cannot be cured, because the bases of his complaint had not been adjudicated by JRP as required by BCO 43-2, and because the complaint to the General Assembly was not timely filed within the 30-day period of BCO 43-3. A concurring opinion by RE Duncan and RE Burnett noted that JRP's commission gave de novo review beyond the Record of the Case and should have narrowly adjudicated whether JRP erred in denying the original complaint.

title: Jennings v. North Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.

Scott to the office of Teaching Elder by a vote of 19-17, which the SJC determined did not satisfy the BCO 34-8 requirement that 'the general sentiment of the Church is strongly in his favor.' The SJC annulled NFP's actions and remanded the case; a lengthy dissent by RE Donahoe argued that BCO 34-8 does not require a super-majority and that the restoration vote is distinct from the evaluation of general sentiment.

summary: Steven Hahn challenged Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery's handling of complaints arising from Christ the King's restriction on his attendance while he sought a psychiatric evaluation. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Session's action was pastoral guidance rather than judicial censure and that no clear error was shown in the lower courts' judgment.

title: Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West. (also Cases 2011-11 and 2011-15)
disposition_detail: Appeal denied; disciplinary judgment affirmed because no clear error was shown

title: Spann v. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church

The SJC requested that Evangel Presbytery direct OMPC to provide a written response to Ms. Spann's concerns.

title: Reese and Bech v. Philadelphia Presbytery

The SJC sustained the complaint, finding that deeming parts of a complaint objectionable is insufficient grounds to rule the whole complaint out of order, though it agreed the proposed amends (removing TE Hsu) were not appropriate.

title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery

title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed Case 2012-01 as judicially out of order on the ground that the action complained against was not in the Record of the Case. A dissenting opinion by three members argued the case should have been adjudicated, contending there was a complain able Session action in the record, as the SJC had itself indicated in the earlier related Case 2011-08; a written objection was also filed regarding TE Aquila's participation as panel chairman given his prior advice to the session at issue.

title: Keating v. Warrior Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Shawn Keating appealed his divestiture without censure by Warrior Presbytery, arguing Presbytery failed to follow BCO 34-10 procedures. The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, finding that Presbytery erred by proceeding to divestiture without first hearing the minister in his own defense, and voided the divestiture while noting Presbytery remained free to proceed again following proper procedures.

title: Charles Tarter v. Evangel Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: TE Tarter appealed his deposition by Evangel Presbytery's Judicial Commission for failure to submit to presbytery authority. The SJC sustained multiple specifications of error — including that the Presbytery's committee had no authority to make certain demands, the indictment was inadequate, and hearsay evidence was improperly admitted — and remanded the case to Evangel Presbytery for constitutionally compliant process or dismissal.

title: Dunn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found TE Dwight Dunn's complaint against Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery to be administratively out of order because the complaint was transmitted to a presbytery commission by the Stated Clerk rather than by motion and action of Presbytery, and because the commission's judgment was never brought back to Presbytery for approval as required by BCO 15-3.

title: Hedman v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: RE Gerald Hedman complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery unconstitutionally adopted five not-guilty verdicts regarding TE Peter Leithart's teachings on baptism, covenants, imputation, justification, and union with Christ. The SJC denied the complaint, finding it was bound by the Record of the Case and that Complainant had not demonstrated clear error on the part of Presbytery, with concurring and dissenting opinions discussing the scope of review, standing, and concerns about Leithart's sacramental theology.

title: Bethel v. Southeast Alabama Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2012-06 administratively out of order on two grounds: the complaint was not filed within the required 30-day period under BCO 43-2, and the complainant (a deacon who was not a commissioner to presbytery on the date of the action complained against) lacked standing under BCO 43-1.

title: William G. Mitchell v. The Presbytery of the Ascension
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.4: the higher court interprets and applies the Church Constitution according to its best ability, without the same deference to the lower court.
summary: RE Mitchell appealed his indefinite suspension from office as Ruling Elder by the Presbytery of the Ascension, arising from allegations he broke a promise to take a sabbatical from Session and failed in his duties as Clerk of Session. The SJC vacated the judgment on Specification No. 2 (promise-breaking) and remanded for possible new trial, and reversed and dismissed Specification No. 6 (clerk duties) as insufficiently serious to warrant trial.

title: Complaint: TE Art Sartorius v. Siouxlands Presbytery 2013-03 Complaint: Mr. G. Rick Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery 2013-06 Appeal: TE Stephen Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery 2013-08 Complaint of
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Art Sartorius and six others against Presbytery of Siouxlands, finding that the Presbytery erred when it approved its Judicial Commission's verdict acquitting TE Gregory Lawrence of five charges related to Federal Vision theology and unconventional views on baptism and apostasy. The SJC identified serious procedural errors, specifically that the Judicial Commission admitted exculpatory post-indictment written statements from the defendant without subjecting them to cross-examination, contrary to BCO 35-5. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with detailed instructions regarding evidence procedures and Presbytery oversight.
topic_tags: rules of evidence in ecclesiastical courts

title: Bennett v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2012-09 administratively out of order because, although the complainant was a PCA member when he filed his original complaint to Presbytery on April 16, 2012, he had transferred to the OPC on April 28, 2012, and therefore lacked standing to bring his complaint to the SJC on August 16, 2012.

title: PCA v. Korean Capital Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The 40th General Assembly had cited Korean Capital Presbytery for failure to respond to exceptions of substance in minutes from October 6, 2008. The SJC noted that Korean Capital Presbytery submitted responses approved by the Presbytery under BCO 10-4, and found those responses acceptable.

title: Tarter v. Evangel
standard_of_review_detail: Decision text is not available locally; standard of review not yet verified.
summary: TE was laboring out of bounds in Ireland. P instructed him on accountability, but he declined requests. Eventually indicted for failure to submit to P authority, found guilty of two charges at trial, and deposed. He

title: Dunn and Pesnell v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Dunn and TE Pesnell complained that Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery erred in adopting its commission's recommendation to institute process and proceed to trial against TE David Swavely for alleged pastoral and spiritual abuse. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that the Presbytery had sufficient authority to proceed to trial and that the errors alleged did not rise to a reversible level.

title: Jackson v. Northwest Georgia
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Case 2013-02 (RE Warren Jackson vs. Northwest Georgia Presbytery) was found to be Administratively Out of Order by the Standing Judicial Commission. No substantive decision on the merits was reached.

title: Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found Marshall's complaint judicially out of order on two grounds: that objections raised during a pending judicial case should be reserved for appeal rather than complaint (BCO 32-14; 42-3), and that no complaint is allowable in a judicial case in which an appeal is pending (BCO 43-1). Three commissioners dissented, arguing BCO 32-14 did not apply before trial commenced and that BCO 43-1's exception is limited to pending appeals, not complaints filed before a trial occurs.

title: the Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The Session of Hope Community Church complained that Central Carolina Presbytery erred in adopting a policy requiring a multi-site session to eventually particularize its second worship site as a distinct new church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO expressly vests the Session with authority over the time and place of worship and the Presbytery's mandatory particularization requirement exceeded its constitutional powers and was annulled.
topic_tags: session authority over time and place of worship

title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
disposition_detail: Administratively out of order; request to assume original jurisdiction not heard
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Steven Hahn asked the SJC to assume original jurisdiction over Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery. The SJC catalog records the matter as administratively out of order, and no merits opinion has been located in the local corpus.

title: Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained TE Gonzales's appeal, reversing and annulling Great Lakes Presbytery's divestiture of him without censure under BCO 34-10, because GLP failed to follow the required procedural steps: it did not record a finding that Gonzales had habitually failed to discharge his official functions, nor determine that his neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church, before proceeding to divestiture. The decision restored Gonzales to good standing in GLP while leaving open GLP's option to pursue proper process under BCO Chapter 31 or 34-10.
topic_tags: lack of acceptance to the Church
habitual failure to perform official functions

title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.
summary: The SJC sustained the Session of FPC North Port's complaint that Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it remanded a previously out-of-order complaint back to the Session and when it directed and instructed the Session to initiate formal ecclesiastical process against a member without following the required steps of BCO 40-5. The Commission held that once the Original CM Complaint was found out of order, there was no matter for Presbytery to carry forward, and any subsequent instructions to the Session to initiate process were null and void.

title: Jackson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because RE Jackson lacked standing as a non-commissioner to the January 2013 Presbytery meeting, but treated his correspondence as a credible BCO 40-5 report of an important delinquency by the Session of Midway Presbyterian Church, remitting the matter to Northwest Georgia Presbytery for constitutional disposition.

title: Marshall v. Pacific
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Appeal by Mr. G. Rick Marshall vs. Pacific Presbytery. Case was withdrawn as prematurely filed and therefore did not proceed to a full SJC decision.

title: Latimer v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: The SJC sustained Rev. Latimer's appeal from his deposition for allegedly pursuing an unbiblical divorce, finding that Presbytery clearly erred because the record contained no conclusive evidence that his divorce filing — made on advice of counsel to protect his children — reflected an intent to divorce rather than a defensive legal measure; two concurring opinions addressed the Presbytery's choice of definite versus indefinite suspension.

title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port, Florida v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.
summary: The SJC sustained the appeal of the Session of FPC North Port from the Presbytery of Southwest Florida's judgment suspending the Session, reversing the judgment in whole and dismissing all charges. The Commission held that Presbytery's citation and trial of the FPC Session for failure to initiate ecclesiastical process against a church member was constitutionally out of order, compounding the same errors identified in Case 2013-07, as Presbytery had failed to follow the required steps of BCO 40-5 before proceeding against the Session.

title: Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed the appeal and suspended the lower court's judgment indefinitely because Pacific Presbytery failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case — a defect that could not be remedied — and rebuked the Presbytery for failure to preserve and transmit trial testimony.

title: Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred in granting TE Hickey an exception to Larger Catechism 177 regarding admission of covenant children to the Lord's Supper. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint, remanding the case to the Presbytery because the record was insufficient to evaluate the minister's particular expression of his paedocommunion view.
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Sanfacon v. Philadelphia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: An inactive ruling elder's complaint to the Session was filed 78 days after the Session action complained against, exceeding the 60-day window of BCO 43-2. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order and voided all subsequent actions.

title: Gearhart v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: An unsigned complaint was filed on TE Gearhart's behalf by a third party without standing, and TE Gearhart did not contact the PCA Clerk until 77 days after the Presbytery action (47 days past the BCO 43-3 deadline). The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order because it was not timely filed and the complainant did not give unqualified ratification.

title: Flesher and Weekly v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found Complaint 2015-03 moot because the issues it raised were adjudicated in the related Appeal 2015-08 (Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery).

title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: John Thompson filed a BCO 43-1 complaint challenging his indictment while his judicial case was still in process before the Session. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order because objections to a trial court's actions must be raised by the defendant during the trial or by appeal after final judgment, not by a separate complaint during the pendency of process.

title: Application of Thompson v. South Florida
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Thompson's BCO 40-5 application alleging grossly unconstitutional proceedings by Granada Presbyterian Church was filed with the SJC before South Florida Presbytery had opportunity to consider it. The SJC dismissed the application as prematurely filed.

title: Presbyterian Church in America v. South Florida Presbytery (Citation)
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC reported that South Florida Presbytery responded to the citation issued by the 43rd General Assembly. The SJC found most responses satisfactory, but found one response unsatisfactory (regarding charges against a TE that were not properly processed under BCO 32-2), and noted an additional exception of substance regarding improper divestiture under BCO 46-8.
topic_tags: citation for failure to respond to exceptions

title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Thompson's complaint to the SJC was prematurely filed before South Florida Presbytery had considered it at its next stated meeting as required by BCO 43-2. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order.

title: Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: TE John Hardie appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Metro Atlanta Presbytery's judicial commission, raising seventeen specifications of error under six categories including procedural irregularities, improper evidence, refusal of indulgence, prejudice, and disproportionate censure. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error in MAP's proceedings and upholding the indefinite suspension.

title: Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Bumgarner, a ruling elder who had been deposed in 2012, filed a BCO 40-5 application in 2015 seeking reversal of the censure after having previously withdrawn his complaint and acknowledged it could not be resubmitted. The SJC dismissed the application as administratively out of order because it sought to re-file a withdrawn complaint and because BCO 40-3 prohibits reversal of judicial censures except by appeal or complaint.

title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Thompson's BCO 40-5 application regarding South Florida Presbytery was found administratively out of order and dismissed because it dealt with proceedings in a judicial case in which a complaint had already been filed, precluding review and control under BCO 40-3.

title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained Thompson's complaint, finding that the Granada Session's judicial commission procedurally erred in imposing excommunication for contumacy before trial because Thompson's behavior did not constitute the immediately censurable kind of contumacy under BCO 32-6.b, and that failing to reach a BCO 38-1 agreement should have led to a trial rather than a pre-trial judgment; the SJC annulled the excommunication and restored the matter to its pre-judgment status as of June 26, 2015.

title: Wills v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Wills's complaint against MAP's September 15, 2015 action declaring a prior complaint administratively out of order was itself administratively out of order, because BCO 43-2 requires a complaint to first be made to the court whose act is alleged to be in error, and MAP had not yet had the opportunity to respond; Duncan, Evans, and Donahoe dissented.

title: Barnes v. Heartland Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Heartland Presbytery sustained the transfer of TE Geoff Smith from an OPC presbytery with stated differences on WCF 19 (the law), without adequately considering or disclosing to the full presbytery that the OPC had declared Smith's views outside the system of doctrine and had restricted him from teaching them. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded to Heartland for further action, with a dissent arguing there was no clear error under BCO 39-3(3).
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Following the SJC's 2014-01 remand directing Ohio Valley Presbytery to 'hear further' from TE Hickey regarding his stated difference on Larger Catechism 177 (paedocommunion), the SJC denied Aven's complaint that OVP failed adequately to comply, finding that OVP did sufficiently hear further from the minister. A significant dissent argued OVP did not satisfy the specific directives from Case 2014-01.
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Robertstad v. North Texas Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because it was initially filed via e-mail rather than by hard copy, and was filed by hard copy only after the thirty-day deadline had passed, contrary to BCO 43-3 and OMSJC 18.10.b which prohibit e-mail filing. A concurring opinion provided extensive history of the 2012 and 2014 amendments to BCO 43-3.

title: Troxell v. Presbytery of the Southwest
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC partially sustained this complaint, annulling Charge 1 (failure to manage household well relating to a June 2014 divorce) because the 15-month delay before process was instituted in September 2015 violated the BCO 32-20 one-year rule with no evidence the offense had recently become flagrant; other specifications of error were denied, and the improper declaration the TE was 'not in good standing' was sustained but not of a nature to annul other actions.

title: Avery and Lewelling v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Avery and Lewelling complained against Nashville Presbytery's denial of their complaint about the Shepherding Committee's investigation of TE Jim Bachmann. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because the actions complained of were those of a committee rather than a court, and the complaint against November 2015 Presbytery action was untimely under BCO 43-2.

title: Doty v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

title: Fordice v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Fordice complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery erred by allowing TE Nathan Lewis to confess under BCO 38-1 and closing the matter without adequate process, after its own investigative committee had found a strong presumption of guilt on 18 allegations. The SJC unanimously sustained the complaint and remanded the case to PNW, finding that while use of BCO 38-1 was not itself error, the approved statement of facts was not 'full' as required because it failed to correlate with the underlying allegations.

title: Korean Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC reviewed Korean Northwest Presbytery's amended and corrected response to exceptions in the review of its records and accepted the response by roll-call vote, with one dissent and one abstention recorded.

title: Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Frazier complained that Nashville Presbytery erred in finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt against TE Scott Sauls regarding his teaching on same-sex attraction; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0-1, concluding NP fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duties, accompanied by several concurring opinions raising procedural and exegetical concerns.

title: Harwell et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed this complaint as judicially out of order because the Harwell complainants had not first properly filed a complaint with Nashville Presbytery—what they filed with Presbytery was in fact a suggestion of charges or call for investigation under BCO 31-2, not a complaint against a court action—and then filed their SJC complaint directly, bypassing the required step of complaining first to the court whose action is alleged to be in error.

title: Daniels et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC declared the complaint moot by a vote of 13-6; the substantial dissenting opinion by six members argued the Commission provided no rationale for the mootness determination and that no constitutional basis for declaring it moot was established.

title: Wills v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue 1 applies BCO 39-3.4 to constitutional interpretation; Issue 2 applies BCO 39-3.3 to discretion and judgment.
summary: TE Tolivar Wills complained that Metro Atlanta Presbytery improperly dissolved Grace North Atlanta Church without following formal judicial process under BCO 40-6. The SJC denied the complaint, ruling that BCO 13-9(f) grants presbytery inherent authority to dissolve a church without mandating any specific procedure, and that the record did not demonstrate clear error in MAP's exercise of its discretion and judgment.

title: Bachmann v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Bachmann appealed Nashville Presbytery's decision to amend its judicial commission's recommended censure of admonition to indefinite suspension; the SJC sustained the appeal, finding NP violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the question and amending the JC's judgment, and rendered the decision that should have been rendered by restoring the JC's censure of admonition.

title: Sartorius v. Siouxlands Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Sartorius complained that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in acquitting TE Greg Lawrence on five charges of holding Federal Vision and non-confessional views on baptism, perseverance, and covenant of works at a second trial (2015); the SJC denied the complaint 22-1, holding that the complainant failed to demonstrate clear error in the trial court's factual finding and that BCO 39-3.2 requires great deference to the lower court's verdict. A concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively discussed standards of appellate review, defendant testimony supporting the acquittal, and raised concerns about due process rights of acquitted persons.

title: Webster & Fowler v. Heritage Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: RE Webster and RE Fowler complained that Heritage Presbytery exceeded its authority when it passed a motion advising the Session of New Covenant Presbyterian Church to postpone ordaining a candidate who might be found unqualified due to non-subscription to infant baptism; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0, finding that Presbytery merely offered advice that Session was free to reject and did not impinge on Session's constitutional authority.
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Dailey v. Heritage Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: RE Dailey complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in upholding its Moderator's ruling that a church member's document was administratively in order as a complaint under BCO 43-3, after the Session had ruled it out of order. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that neither triggering condition of BCO 43-3 was met because the Session's ruling that the document did not qualify as a BCO 43-1 complaint was not equivalent to denying it, and the Session had considered and responded to the matter in a timely manner. A substantial dissent argued for a broader interpretation of 'fails to consider' in BCO 43-3.

title: Postles v. Heritage Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: RE Postles complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in acting on an ad interim committee recommendation to charge a teaching elder with violating ordination vows 6 and 7 and appointing a prosecutor. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that a committee may recommend judicial action without special authorization (distinguishing from a commission under BCO 15-3), that BCO 31-2 procedures were properly followed, and that the language used by Presbytery in its motion was constitutionally sufficient to institute process.

title: Daniels et al. v. Nashville Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Case listed as docket entry 'Complaint of RE Daniels, et al. v. Nashville Presbytery' but determined by the SJC to be administratively out of order and removed from consideration without decision.

title: BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: BCO 40-5 report filed by RE John B. Thompson. The case was withdrawn before consideration by the SJC. Listed in the docket of cases filed during the 2017 docket year, which was reported to the 46th General Assembly in 2018.

title: BCO 40-5 report of TE James Bachman. Ruled
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: BCO 40-5 report of Teaching Elder James Bachman. The Standing Judicial Commission determined this case to be out of order and did not render a substantive decision on the merits.

title: Request for Reference from Blue Ridge Presbytery
disposition_detail: reference denied; complaint returned to presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Blue Ridge Presbytery requested that the Standing Judicial Commission hear and decide a complaint because of claimed bias and constitutional questions. The SJC denied the request for reference, holding that the record did not demonstrate affirmative bias, serious division, constitutional questions, or delicate issues that would warrant reference under BCO 41-2. The presbytery was directed to hear and decide the complaint itself.

title: Clements v. Blue Ridge Presbytery (Complaint)
disposition_detail: reference denied; complaint returned to presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Companion complaint to 2017-06; the SJC answered this complaint by reference to its decision denying the request for reference in 2017-06, directing Blue Ridge Presbytery to hear and decide the matter.

title: BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson. Ruled
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson listed in SJC docket as ruled out of order. No full opinion published.

title: BCO 40-5 report of RE John B. Thompson. Ruled
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: A BCO 40-5 report filed by RE John B. Thompson was determined to be out of order by the SJC. No written opinion was issued, and the case appears only in the docket listing indicating its administrative dismissal.

title: In re Korean Eastern Presbytery
disposition_detail: responses accepted; referred to Review Committee
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC Commission recognized that Korean Eastern Presbytery complied with its citation, provided required materials under BCO 40-1, and referred those materials to the Committee for Review of Presbytery Records.

title: In re Korean Southwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: responses accepted; referred to Review Committee
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Standing Judicial Commission voted unanimously to accept responses from Korean Southwest Presbytery as complying with the Commission's citation, forwarding those responses to the Committee for Review of Presbytery Records for further consideration.
