title: In re Platte Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: responses accepted; referred to Review Committee
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Standing Judicial Commission voted unanimously to accept responses from Platte Valley Presbytery, which had been approved by the presbytery, as complying with the SJC citation and forwarded those responses to the Review of Presbytery Records Committee.

title: Tripp v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Withdrawn before decision; no merits disposition
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: TE David Tripp’s appeal against Ohio Valley Presbytery was withdrawn before the SJC issued a decision. No opinion text or merits disposition is recorded in the official case listing.

title: Glen Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained in part; censures reversed and replaced with admonition; related complaint moot
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: RE Glen Mapes appealed his conviction and censures by a temporary session of New Hope Christian Church. The SJC sustained the appeal in part, affirming the finding that he failed to submit to church government but reversing the excessive suspension and deposition and replacing them with admonition; the related complaint was moot after the church left the PCA.

title: Lewis v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled that Anna Lewis's BCO 40-5 report filed directly with the SJC was out of order, holding that the SJC's only responsibility under Chapter 40 arises upon referral from the General Assembly per RAO 16-10.c. Six members dissented, arguing the SJC has historically exercised direct jurisdiction over BCO 40-5 reports and that the majority's interpretation was overly narrow and a departure from settled precedent.

title: Durand v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC unanimously ruled that Geoffrey Durand's BCO 31-2 report affecting Christian character was administratively out of order and could not be put in order, as there is no constitutional provision for the SJC to receive a BCO 31-2 report directly.

title: Mapes v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint by RE Glen Mapes et al. not judicially in order because it was rendered moot: the remedy sought (a congregational meeting to vote on leaving the PCA) was accomplished when the presbytery voted to dismiss the congregation and the congregation consented. Three members dissented.

title: McKay v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC unanimously ruled the complaint by TE David McKay was administratively out of order because the e-mail transmitted to the clerk of the lower court did not meet BCO 43-3's requirement for proper notice.

title: Edwards v. North Texas Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled the complaint by Jared Edwards was administratively out of order and could not be put in order because the case was never filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below, as required by BCO 42-4 and 43-2.

title: Dodson et al. v. Ohio Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.; BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

title: Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Daniel Schrock and others complained that Philadelphia Presbytery failed to properly judge and record the nature of TE Larry Smith's views on the continuation of spiritual gifts of prophecy and tongues when it admitted him by transfer, as required by BCO 21-4e,f and RAO 16-3.e.5. The SJC sustained the complaint by a vote of 14-5-2 and remanded the matter to Presbytery to receive a written statement from TE Smith and make a proper determination, with a substantial dissent arguing the Presbytery had in fact complied with the Constitution and that RAO 16-3.e.5 is not part of the BCO.
topic_tags: fundamentals of the system of doctrine

title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: The SJC sustained the complaint, ruling that a Session erred by prescreening and eliminating a deacon's nomination for ruling elder before the mandatory instruction and examination process required by BCO 24-1. The decision held that BCO 24-1's language is mandatory and that sessions cannot add a preliminary vetting step that bypasses the required sequence of instruction and examination.

title: Williams v. Chesapeake Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Chesapeake Presbytery's PJC attempted to convert a BCO 32 case of process into a BCO 38-1 case without process after TE Williams partially pled guilty, confusing the two distinct procedures. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled the Presbytery's action, finding the conflation of BCO 32 and 38-1 violated the due process rights of the accused.
topic_tags: case of process vs case without process

title: Goggan v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Mr. Goggan was excommunicated by a Missouri Presbytery judicial commission after a trial on charges of bearing false witness, perpetuating a faction, and other offenses. The SJC denied his appeal, finding he failed to demonstrate sufficient reason to sustain any of the alleged errors.

title: Presbyterian Church in America v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.
summary: The SJC ruled that the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley erred in approving a Session's erasure of a member's name from the roll under BCO 38-4 after she pled not guilty to a charge of failing to submit to church government and pursued divorce contrary to the Session's counsel. The SJC found multiple constitutional errors including improper conflation of a not-guilty plea with refusal to submit, failure to consider whether the member would fulfill vows in another branch of the church, failure to notify the member of her erasure, and proceeding to a case without process after dropping formal charges.

title: Fozard v. North Texas Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Mr. Chandler Fozard complained that Fort Worth Presbyterian Church's policy restricting the integration of special case felons (including sex offenders) into the congregation violated Scripture. The SJC denied the complaint 20-1, finding the complainant had not demonstrated the Session violated Scripture or the Constitution, while criticizing the Session's arguments from BCO Preliminary Principles 1 and 2 as improper.

title: Ganzel v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Neal Ganzel appealed his conviction and six-month suspension by Central Florida Presbytery for abuse of spiritual authority and related charges. The SJC unanimously sustained both specifications of error, finding that CFP violated BCO 32-20's one-year statute of limitations for most charges and committed numerous procedural missteps that rendered the disciplinary process significantly flawed and prejudicial, reversing the entire censure.

title: Mueller v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.
summary: RE Mueller complained that the Redlands Community Church Session reaffirmed a practice of fencing the Lord's Table contrary to BCO 58-4, but the SJC found the Session took no action because the relevant motion failed for lack of a second. The complaint was denied, with a concurring opinion emphasizing that BCO 58-4's fencing requirement remains a constitutional obligation.

title: Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE Evans under BCO 38-1 without properly securing his approval of the full statement of facts, as the Investigative Committee's report added additional adverse facts he had not seen or approved. The SJC sustained the complaints of Evans and Pitts et al., annulled the deposition, and remanded the matter to AZP for action consistent with BCO 38-1 requirements; a lengthy concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively analyzed BCO 38-1 confession procedures.

title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The adopted opinion applies BCO 39-3.3 to the Session's exercise of discretion and judgment; the dissent argues for BCO 39-3.4 but does not alter the majority holding.
summary: The SJC denied a complaint by an ordained Deacon whose nomination for re-election was not advanced by the Session, holding that the Session's exercise of discretion in evaluating a candidate's eligibility for office did not constitute clear error requiring reversal. The dissent argued the proper standard of review was BCO 39-3.4 (de novo for constitutional interpretation), not 39-3.3 (great deference), because the Session applied extra-biblical and extra-constitutional attendance standards in blocking re-election.

title: Gendy v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained a complaint finding that Central Florida Presbytery erred in ruling that Ms. Gendy lacked standing to complain about her removal from church membership under BCO 38-4, holding that a member facing removal retains standing to challenge that removal. The case was remanded to Presbytery to consider the original complaint regarding whether the Session had properly applied BCO 38-3a and 38-4.

title: Yoo et al. v. Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found this complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it because no documentation was received showing the complaint was first made to the presbytery whose act was alleged to be in error, and the proper court for the charges included was the Presbytery.

title: In the matter of PCA v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: No appellate standard applies to this original-jurisdiction request or other non-appellate proceeding.
summary: The SJC answered BCO 34-1 requests from three presbyteries to assume original jurisdiction by reference to the SJC's prior decisions in Case 2020-12 and Case 2020-05, both involving TE Ryan Speck v. Missouri Presbytery. RE Mel Duncan requested that his negative vote be recorded.

title: Marusich v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: The SJC remanded the case to Central Indiana Presbytery with instructions to appoint a committee to reinvestigate under BCO 31-2, after its non-judicial commission declined to find a strong presumption of guilt against an accused teaching elder. The dissent argued the SJC failed to give proper great deference under BCO 39-3.3 to the presbytery's investigative commission's discretionary judgment declining to indict, and that the BCO does not require the investigative procedures ordered by the Decision.

title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The adopted opinion resolves the complaint on the constitutional criteria and procedural errors identified, without stating a distinct BCO 39-3 standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part TE Ryan Speck's complaint against Missouri Presbytery's December 2019 adoption of six theological judgments regarding the 2018 Revoice Conference hosted by Memorial Presbyterian Church, ruling that MOP applied an incorrect constitutional standard (BCO 34-5 'vitals of religion') rather than the proper BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f) criteria, and failed to take adequate action with respect to erroneous teachings identified by its own committees regarding terminology (TJ 2), the 'gay beneath the gay' (TJ 3), and spiritual friendships (TJ 5); the matter was remanded to MOP with instructions for a new hearing. Dissenting opinions were filed by RE John D. Pickering and TE David F. Coffin, Jr., who argued that the SJC improperly raised an issue not presented by either party in violation of BCO 39-3.1.

title: Gordon v. Southern New England Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.
summary: Mr. Gordon was excommunicated by a PCA Session after his former OPC congregation joined the PCA against his expressed wishes; he contended the PCA Session lacked jurisdiction over him. The SJC majority denied his appeal affirming the excommunication, while a four-member dissent argued the SJC should have ruled the case out of order for lack of jurisdiction and standing, as Gordon never voluntarily became a PCA member.

title: Wilbourne v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Pacific Presbytery's judicial commission read a prejudicial six-page report prior to TE Wilbourne's BCO 38-1 confession of guilt, then deposed him; the SJC sustained the complaint, annulled the deposition, and recommended treating his 17-month effective suspension as definite suspension from office. Complaints 2020-08 and 2020-09 by fellow TEs and the Session of Pacific Crossroads Church were sustained by reference to this decision.

title: Gendall, Hightower, and Lien v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Three Teaching Elders complained against Pacific Presbytery's handling of TE Wilbourne's BCO 38-1 confession and subsequent deposition. The SJC sustained the complaints by reference to its decision in Case 2020-07.

title: Oxbalt et al. v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: RE Sean Ozbalt and RE Erin Barr filed complaints challenging Pacific Presbytery's handling of TE Rankin Wilbourne's case. The SJC sustained the complaints, finding that the reading of a judicial commission report not agreed upon by the accused violated BCO 38-1, that the sins were not base and flagitious, and that procedural constitutional violations occurred. The SJC annulled the censure of deposition and recommended treating the 17-month censure as a definite suspension from office.

title: Eagle v. Savannah River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2020-10 administratively out of order as prematurely filed because Presbytery had not yet completed its hearing on the complaint; the complainant's time to elevate was reset.

title: McWilliams v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The complainant requested to withdraw and abandon his complaint, which the SJC approved unanimously.

title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Ryan Speck complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in declining to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE Greg Johnson regarding four allegations arising from his involvement in and teaching at the Revoice 2018 conference; the SJC sustained the complaint in part on Issue 1 (particularly regarding Theological Judgments 2, 3, and 5 about terminology, gay identity, and spiritual friendship), denied Issues 2 and 3, and remanded the matter to Missouri Presbytery for a new hearing on specific questions.

title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed this complaint as administratively out of order because Mr. Benyola lacked standing to complain against a presbytery action, as he was neither a teaching elder member of that presbytery nor a ruling elder commissioner representing a member church at the September 18, 2020 meeting where the presbytery considered and denied the complaint.

title: Michelson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2021-01 administratively out of order as prematurely filed because Presbytery had not yet completed its hearing on the complaint; the complainant's time to elevate was reset.

title: Tippins v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: On a BCO 40-5 request, the SJC advised that the matter should be referred to the General Assembly's Review of Presbytery Records Committee, with three members dissenting.

title: DeJong v. Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part RE DeJong's complaint against Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church (Rocky Mountain Presbytery), upholding Session's creation of a Judicial Commission and its recommendation to remove term limit restrictions for ruling elders, but annulling Session's creation of a Governance Commission because two provisions of the governing document unconstitutionally allowed the commission to function like the Session itself, exceeding the limits placed on commissions by BCO 15-1.

title: Eudaly and Light v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC ruled Case 2021-05 administratively out of order because the complainants had affiliated with another branch of the visible church on February 9, 2020, losing PCA jurisdiction and therefore lacking standing to file the complaint.

title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: The SJC denied most specifications of a complaint filed by TE Herron and others against Central Indiana Presbytery's investigative and suspension procedures, but sustained the complaint on the point that Presbytery improperly denied Herron access to Presbytery minutes while under process. The decision includes extensive discussion of pre-trial BCO 43-1 complaints ('interlocutory appeals') and the proper scope of BCO 31-10 administrative suspensions.

title: Acree v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: RE Acree attempted to file a BCO 43-1 complaint with Presbytery against an action taken at a Presbytery meeting he did not attend as a commissioner. The SJC found the case administratively out of order because Acree lacked standing, not having been a commissioner at the meeting where the action was taken.

title: Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery
disposition_detail: Citation and response process; no merits disposition in this record
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC cited Korean Southwest Orange County Presbytery to respond to an exception in the review of its records. When no adopted response had arrived by the March 3, 2022 meeting, the SJC allowed time for the presbytery to adopt and file one and warned that failure could lead to a further appearance; no merits disposition appears in this record.

title: Park et al. v. Korean Central Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained a complaint against Korean Central Presbytery for administering a censure to a teaching elder before an indictment was drawn, in violation of BCO 32-3, and declared the underlying matter moot given that events occurred 21 years prior and the victim declined to participate. A concurring opinion argued the case should have been remanded to Presbytery for further action, and a dissenting opinion objected to declaring the case moot.

title: Michelson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because it targeted actions of a congregational meeting rather than any act or decision of a court of the Church, as required by BCO 43-1. A dissenting opinion by RE Jack Wilson and seven others argued that the Complainants had sufficiently identified an act of the Session (calling the congregational meeting with the stated purposes) to present a justiciable issue.

title: Dudt v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: RE Dudt was convicted and suspended from office by the Midway Presbyterian Church Session for emailing the congregation an SJC decision and expressing disagreement with a Session action, which the Session characterized as violating his ordination vows. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversing in whole and rendering a verdict of not guilty, finding that the Session had no constitutional authority to forbid Dudt from distributing the SJC decision and that the charges of false statements were not proven. A concurring opinion by several judges cautioned against elders emailing congregations in disagreement with Session decisions.

title: Herron et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: This complaint was postponed pending resolution of Case 2022-10 (PCA v. Herron trial) per the SJC's June 2022 instruction in Case 2021-06, and the SJC ruled it be decided by reference to the April 5, 2023 Final Decision in Case 2022-10.

title: Barber et al. v. Central Indiana Presbytery

summary: This complaint was postponed pending resolution of Case 2022-10 (PCA v. Herron trial) per the SJC's June 2022 instruction in Case 2021-06, and the SJC ruled it be decided by reference to the April 5, 2023 Final Decision in Case 2022-10.

title: Eagle v. Savannah River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Complaint by Eric Eagle and others against Savannah River Presbytery, found administratively out of order by the SJC Officers because the complaint was not timely filed within thirty days of the later of the SJC's notification (October 21, 2021) or Presbytery's ruling (October 20, 2020), as required by BCO 43-3. The case was dismissed on a unanimous 19-0-0 vote.

title: Herron & Baysinger v. Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: This complaint was postponed pending resolution of Case 2022-10 (PCA v. Herron trial) per the SJC's June 2022 instruction in Case 2021-06, and the SJC ruled it be decided by reference to the April 5, 2023 Final Decision in Case 2022-10.

title: Klett et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to find that TE Larry Smith's views affirming continuing gifts of prophecy and tongues (as a 'third category of revelation' beyond special and general revelation) were out of accord with the fundamentals of the system of doctrine because hostile to it, as required by BCO 21-4.f. The case continues past this window's end page.

title: Sheppard v. Highlands Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: TE Craig Sheppard complained that Highlands Presbytery erred by conflating judicial and pastoral procedures after finding a strong presumption of guilt, and by failing to institute process within one year as required by BCO 32-20. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that BCO 31-2 mandates process upon finding a strong presumption of guilt, and that Presbytery was debarred from prosecution because the alleged offense occurred in 2017 and timely process was never instituted; three members dissented on the BCO 32-20 issue, arguing it was not a true statute of limitations and that the matter was never a 'case of scandal.'

title: Crouse et al. v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found this complaint against Northwest Georgia Presbytery out of order and moot because the Session had dismissed all charges and the ruling elders who were subjects of process had voluntarily resigned and had their calls dissolved before the SJC acted. The complaint was accordingly dismissed unanimously.

title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Complainants withdrew this Complaint on July 18, 2022, and the SJC noted such on October 20, 2022. No substantive decision was issued.

title: Harrell et al. v. Covenant Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.; BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: Seven members of a PCA mission church were tried and censured by a provisional Session for opposing the organizing minister's continuation as permanent pastor. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the convictions, holding that the indictments lacked required specificity under BCO 32-5, that the accused had no sinned against the fifth or ninth commandment by expressing opinions about ministerial suitability, and that the right to choose a pastor belongs to the congregation—not the provisional Session. A concurring opinion addressed indictment requirements, standard of review in appeals, and congregational rights in mission church minister selection.

title: David Snoke v. Pittsburgh Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and unable to be put in order because RE Snoke lacked standing to file a complaint against presbytery action, as he was not a commissioner from his church to the presbytery meeting where the challenged action occurred. The SJC voted 20-1 to dismiss (Sartorius dissenting).

title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because Mr. Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and thus lacked standing. The SJC approved the dismissal unanimously 23-0.

title: Presbyterian Church in America v. TE Daniel Herron
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.
summary: The SJC conducted a full 42-hour trial of TE Daniel Herron of Central Indiana Presbytery on charges arising from allegations of sexual harassment and bullying, referred to the SJC by CIP under BCO 41. The SJC acquitted TE Herron on all charges, removed all censures and administrative suspensions imposed by CIP, and restored him to good standing as a PCA minister.

title: BCO 34-1 Petitions re: Central Indiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC decided the BCO 34-1 petitions regarding Central Indiana Presbytery by reference to the April 5, 2023 final decision in Case 2022-10 (PCA v. Herron), having previously postponed consideration of these petitions until after the Herron trial concluded.

title: BCO 34-1 Petitions re: Missouri Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Two overtures from Southeast Alabama and Grace Presbyteries sought GA assumption of original jurisdiction over TE Greg Johnson of Missouri Presbytery for alleged doctrinal errors; the SJC dismissed the petitions (22-1) because TE Johnson and Memorial Presbyterian Church withdrew from the PCA in December 2022, depriving the PCA of jurisdiction.

title: Miller v. Hills & Plains Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found Mr. Miller's complaint administratively out of order (22-0) because he filed it with the Session six months after the Session's action (May 19, 2021), well beyond the 60-day deadline required by BCO 43-1.

title: Oh v. Korean Southeast Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint withdrawn; dismissed without merits decision
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: TE Sung Bok Oh withdrew his complaint against Korean Southeast Presbytery on August 29, 2022. The SJC therefore recorded a procedural disposition without reaching the merits of the complaint.

title: Murdock v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order (23-0) because complainant RE Terry Murdock died on November 15, 2022, and no other party had joined the original complaint.

title: Michelson et al. v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot (23-0) because the Session had dismissed all charges against the three Ruling Elders involved and those REs voluntarily resigned and had their calls dissolved on July 23, 2022, settling the underlying dispute.

title: Peter Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery (three complaints)
disposition_detail: Complaints administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: Peter Benyola's three complaints against Central Florida Presbytery were found administratively out of order because he was no longer a member of a PCA congregation and therefore lacked standing; the SJC did not reach the merits.

title: Wilson et al. v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC found the complaint judicially out of order (20-2) because BCO 43-1 permits complaints only against acts of a court of the church, not against actions taken in a congregational meeting; the case involved complainants who alleged minor communicant members were wrongly prevented from voting on accepting their associate pastor's resignation, with concurring and dissenting opinions extensively addressing the question of minor communicant suffrage rights and the scope of BCO 43 jurisdiction.

title: Senters v. Savannah River Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE David Senters complained that Savannah River Presbytery erred by judging TE Stamberg's stated difference with WCF 21.3 regarding the gift of tongues as 'not a difference' during a transfer examination. The SJC denied the procedural part of the complaint but sustained the confessional part, finding it was error to conclude Stamberg's view on continuing tongues was not a difference with WCF 1.1 and 1.6, and remanded to Presbytery for further action.

title: Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings.
summary: RE Tom Turner complained against South Florida Presbytery's action finding the Session of Cross Community Church guilty of important delinquencies related to alleged sexual abuse incidents involving the pastor's sons, without formal judicial process. The SJC denied the complaint as to Presbytery's right to investigate under BCO 40-4, but sustained it as to the finding of guilt and imposed censures, holding that formal judicial process (indictment, plea, and trial) under BCO 40-6 was required before findings of guilt could be entered, and remanded to Presbytery.

title: Woodham v. South Florida Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: Issue-level standards: BCO 39-3.2: factual findings receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.; BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: TE Michael Woodham complained that South Florida Presbytery erred by excommunicating a Teaching Elder it had previously deposed without first assigning him to membership in a particular church as required by BCO 46-8. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that Presbytery retained jurisdiction over a deposed minister until transfer to a local church was completed, and that Presbytery's efforts to implement BCO 46-8 showed no clear error; two concurring opinions (RE Donahoe and RE Eggert) offered alternative reasoning regarding the scope of Presbytery's residual jurisdiction.

title: Hann v. Pee Dee Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed Mrs. Hann's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery because she lacked standing, not being subject to the jurisdiction of the Presbytery. The ruling noted that Presbytery's ongoing investigation was not stayed by this ruling.
topic_tags: complainant not subject to presbytery jurisdiction

title: Reynolds v. Pee Dee Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The SJC dismissed Mrs. Reynolds's complaint against Pee Dee Presbytery as untimely, finding it was filed more than sixty days after the Session action in question. The ruling expressly reserved questions about whether she might bring charges as an injured party under BCO 31-5.

title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Tennessee Valley Presbytery approved without exception Session minutes planning a youth group Super Bowl Party on Sunday; the SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in its constitutional interpretation. A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

title: Hyland v. Chicago Metro Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: A terminated church employee filed a complaint against Chicago Metro Presbytery after Presbytery declined to indict the pastors she accused, but Presbytery ruled her complaint out of order for lack of standing under BCO 43-1. The SJC, voting 12-12, left the Presbytery's decision standing, finding the complaint judicially out of order because the complainant lacked standing to file a BCO 43-1 complaint against Presbytery.

title: Knox Baird et al. v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaints sustained in the main; one specification denied and one not reached
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Knox Baird and other elders challenged Grace Presbytery's handling of complaints, BCO 40-5 review requests, document demands, and a stay of pending trials arising from conflict at First Presbyterian Church of Hattiesburg. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main—finding the Blue Hen complaint moot and improperly taken up, the document directive partly overbroad, and the stay improper—while rejecting one complaint and not reaching impartiality; concurring opinions were recorded.

title: Evans v. Arizona Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE John Evans appealed Arizona Presbytery's vote to divest him of his office without censure under BCO 34-10, after he had already affiliated with the Evangelical Presbyterian Church in England and Wales and notified the Presbytery of his withdrawal. The SJC unanimously sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery's action, holding that Evans had withdrawn from Presbytery's jurisdiction under BCO 38-3a before the divestiture proceedings began, and instructed the Presbytery to record the irregularity, acknowledge his new membership, and remove his name from the roll.

title: Myers v. Illiana Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

title: Martinez & Cook v. Pacific Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 39-3.3: matters of discretion and judgment receive great deference; reversal requires clear error.
summary: REs Martinez and Cook complained that Pacific Presbytery erred by tasking its Shepherding Committee to follow up with Valley Presbyterian Church's Session after a dispute about doxologies in worship, alleging this exceeded Presbytery's jurisdictional authority. The SJC denied the complaint on Issue 1 (finding no BCO violation in the visitation itself) but sustained it on Issue 2, concluding Presbytery made clear errors of judgment by sending the Shepherding Committee without sufficiently clear instructions or adequate notice.

title: Psiaki v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

title: BCO 40-5 Matter re Metropolitan NY
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: The Standing Judicial Commission ruled on a matter involving Metropolitan New York Presbytery's handling of a session that permitted a woman to expound Scripture during worship and held services without sermons. The SJC remitted the matter to the Presbytery to complete its work and report to the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, while critiquing the procedural manner in which the matter was referred to the SJC.

title: BCO 40-5 Matter re NW Georgia
disposition_detail: BCO 40-5 ruling found egregious constitutional error; proceedings were stayed and terminated, but requested annulment was denied.
standard_of_review_detail: BCO 40-5: important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings; the SJC found egregious constitutional error and addressed the requested relief.
summary: The SJC, pursuant to citation by the 50th General Assembly under BCO 40-5, found that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred egregiously in approving calls and installing three candidates as associate pastors through a constitutionally deficient election process (slate voting, standing vote, failure to record number of voters present). The SJC stayed all further proceedings and declined to annul the installations, finding no PCA precedent for such relief.

title: Tom Turner v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order for lack of standing
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: RE Tom Turner challenged South Florida Presbytery's handling of matters involving Cross Community Church and the discipline of its pastor after the church voted to disaffiliate from the PCA. The SJC ruled the complaints administratively out of order for lack of standing because the church had already disaffiliated, a conclusion opposed by two dissenting commissioners.

title: Huffman v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
standard_of_review_detail: The matter was resolved procedurally, administratively, abandoned, dismissed, or referred before merits review.
summary: TE Huffman filed an appeal after the 50th GA amended BCO 38-1 to change the remedy from complaint to appeal, but his case originated and was nearly complete under the prior rule allowing complaint. The SJC found the case judicially out of order and remanded to Tennessee Valley Presbytery to adjudicate as a complaint under the then-existing rule, resetting the clock for presbytery action.

title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal sustained; divestiture reversed and ministers returned to good standing
standard_of_review_detail: Decision text is not available locally; standard of review not yet verified.
summary: TEs Felipe Assis and Carter Brown appealed South Florida Presbytery's decision to divest them without censure after their churches left the PCA and they remained without transferred credentials. The SJC sustained the appeal, holding that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 did not authorize the divestiture on these facts, returned the ministers to good standing, and directed Presbytery to dissolve the existing calls and pursue a constitutionally appropriate course; two specifications could not be judged on the record.

title: David C. Lachman et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: sustained on all specifications; annulled action of Philadelphia Presbytery and instructed presbytery to advise session that physical cruelty does not constitute biblical grounds for divorce
standard_of_review_detail: The available decision does not state a distinct standard of review.
summary: Case concerns whether Philadelphia Presbytery properly failed to sustain a judicial commission judgment regarding session's decision that physical cruelty constitutes biblical grounds for divorce. All three specifications sustained unanimously or nearly unanimously.
